1Basic Introduction to Embedded Platform

An embedded system is a small computer built into a device to do one dedicated job, like a washing machine or a smart watch. An embedded platform such as Arduino puts a microcontroller, power circuit, USB interface and pin headers on one board.

Key points

  • Microcontroller (MCU): one chip with CPU, memory and I/O pins. Uno uses the ATmega328P.
  • Arduino Uno: 14 digital pins (6 PWM), 6 analog inputs, 16 MHz, 32 KB flash, 2 KB SRAM, 5 V.
  • setup() runs once at start; loop() repeats forever.

Code

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(9600);
  Serial.println("Hello, Embedded World!");
}
void loop() { }
FunctionPurpose
pinMode(pin, mode)Set a pin as INPUT, OUTPUT or INPUT_PULLUP
digitalWrite / digitalReadWrite or read HIGH (5 V) / LOW (0 V)
analogRead(pin)Read 0 to 1023 from A0 to A5
analogWrite(pin, v)PWM output, 0 to 255
delay(ms)Pause the program
Quick viva questions
  • Microcontroller vs microprocessor?
  • Why do we need setup() and loop()?
  • Which Arduino pins support PWM?
2LED Blinking in Various Patterns

Blinking an LED is the “Hello World” of embedded systems. It teaches digital output, timing and how loops and arrays build patterns.

Key points

  • LED legs: anode (+, longer) and cathode (−, shorter).
  • Always use a series resistor (220 to 330 Ω): R = (5 − 2) / 0.015 ≈ 200 Ω.
  • Wiring: Arduino pin → resistor → LED anode; cathode → GND.

Code

int leds[] = {2, 3, 4, 5};
void setup() {
  for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) pinMode(leds[i], OUTPUT);
}
void loop() {
  for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    digitalWrite(leds[i], HIGH);
    delay(300);
    digitalWrite(leds[i], LOW);
  }
}
PatternIdea
Blink / AlternateAll LEDs on and off together, or odd/even swapping
ChaserTurn LEDs on one by one with a for loop
Fade (PWM)analogWrite() from 0 to 255 changes brightness
Quick viva questions
  • Why is a resistor needed with an LED?
  • What is PWM and how does it dim an LED?
  • How can an array shorten pattern code?
3Analog Sensor Interfacing

The real world is analog. The Arduino ADC converts 0 to 5 V into a number from 0 to 1023 (10-bit), so sensors like LDRs, LM35 and potentiometers can be read.

Key points

  • Resolution: 5 V / 1024 ≈ 4.88 mV per step.
  • Voltage = analogRead(pin) × 5.0 / 1023.
  • map() rescales a reading, e.g. 0–1023 to 0–255 for PWM.
  • Resistive sensors are read through a voltage divider.

Code

int potPin = A0, ledPin = 10;
void setup() { pinMode(ledPin, OUTPUT); Serial.begin(9600); }
void loop() {
  int pot = analogRead(potPin);
  int br = map(pot, 0, 1023, 0, 255);
  analogWrite(ledPin, br);   // brightness
  Serial.println(pot);
  delay(50);
}
Quick viva questions
  • Range of analogRead() on Uno?
  • Why use a voltage divider with an LDR?
  • How can ADC resolution be improved?
4LCD and Bluetooth Interfacing

A 16×2 LCD shows 16 characters on 2 lines. HC-05 is a Bluetooth serial module that lets the Arduino talk to a phone.

Key points

  • LCD uses the LiquidCrystal library in 4-bit mode (RS, E, D4–D7); a 10k pot on V0 sets contrast.
  • HC-05 uses UART at 9600 baud; pairing PIN is 1234 or 0000.
  • SoftwareSerial makes pins 8 and 9 a spare serial port.
  • HC-05 RX is 3.3 V, so use a 1k/2k divider on the Arduino TX line.

Code

#include <LiquidCrystal.h>
#include <SoftwareSerial.h>
LiquidCrystal lcd(12, 11, 5, 4, 3, 2);
SoftwareSerial bt(8, 9);
void setup() { lcd.begin(16, 2); bt.begin(9600); lcd.print("BT Ready"); }
void loop() {
  if (bt.available()) {
    char c = bt.read();
    lcd.clear(); lcd.print("Got: "); lcd.print(c);
  }
}
Quick viva questions
  • Why is the LCD used in 4-bit mode?
  • What is baud rate?
  • Why do we need SoftwareSerial?
5IR and Ultrasonic Sensor Integration

Distance and obstacle sensors are the eyes of robots. The two common ones are the IR obstacle sensor and the HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor.

Key points

  • Ultrasonic distance = time × 0.034 / 2 cm (sound goes and returns).
  • IR module output is usually LOW when an obstacle is detected.

Code

const int trig = 9, echo = 10;
void setup() { pinMode(trig, OUTPUT); pinMode(echo, INPUT); Serial.begin(9600); }
void loop() {
  digitalWrite(trig, LOW);  delayMicroseconds(2);
  digitalWrite(trig, HIGH); delayMicroseconds(10);
  digitalWrite(trig, LOW);
  long t = pulseIn(echo, HIGH);
  Serial.print(t * 0.034 / 2); Serial.println(" cm");
  delay(300);
}
FeatureIR sensorUltrasonic (HC-SR04)
PrincipleReflected infrared lightTime of flight of sound (40 kHz)
RangeAbout 2 to 30 cmAbout 2 to 400 cm
OutputDigital (LOW = obstacle)Pulse width on ECHO pin
Weak spotSunlight, black surfacesSoft or angled surfaces
UseLine follower, counterDistance meter, parking sensor
Quick viva questions
  • Why is the measured time divided by 2?
  • Speed of sound in cm per microsecond?
  • Where would you use IR instead of ultrasonic?
6Basic of App Building

MIT App Inventor is a free, block-based tool that runs in the browser and builds an installable APK.

Key points

  • Designer: drag Buttons, Labels, Sliders, ListPicker onto the screen.
  • Blocks: snap event blocks (when Button1.Click) to action blocks.
  • Test live with the AI2 Companion app, then Build → Android App (.apk).
  • Key ideas: event-driven programming, variables, permissions.
Quick viva questions
  • What is an APK?
  • What is event-driven programming?
  • Name three Designer components.
7App Integration with Embedded Platform

The phone app and Arduino exchange data over Bluetooth. The app sends commands and the Arduino can send sensor values back.

Key points

  • Add BluetoothClient and a ListPicker to choose the paired HC-05.
  • Buttons send a character with SendText or Send1ByteNumber.
  • The Arduino reads it with bt.read() and acts using if / switch.
  • Both sides must use the same baud rate (9600).

Code

#include <SoftwareSerial.h>
SoftwareSerial bt(8, 9);
void setup() { pinMode(13, OUTPUT); bt.begin(9600); }
void loop() {
  if (bt.available()) {
    char c = bt.read();
    if (c == '1') digitalWrite(13, HIGH);
    if (c == '0') digitalWrite(13, LOW);
  }
}
Quick viva questions
  • What if baud rates do not match?
  • How can sensor values be shown in the app?
  • Why pair the HC-05 first?
8Cloud Integration with App

IoT connects devices to the internet. Sensor data goes to the cloud, is stored and visualised, and can be viewed anywhere.

Key points

  • Uno has no Wi-Fi, so use ESP8266 / ESP32.
  • Steps: create account and channel, copy the API key, add it to code, upload and view data online.
  • Protocols: HTTP (REST) and MQTT (publish/subscribe).
  • Never share your API key publicly.
PlatformTypeUse
BlynkIoT app + cloudMobile dashboard for ESP32
ThingSpeakCloud analyticsLog data and plot live graphs
FirebaseRealtime databaseSync data with a custom app
Quick viva questions
  • What is IoT?
  • Why ESP32 instead of Uno here?
  • HTTP vs MQTT?
9Basic of 3D Printing

3D printing builds an object layer by layer. Student printers use FDM: melted filament pushed through a nozzle.

Key points

  • Workflow: design (Tinkercad, Fusion 360) → export STL → slice (Cura, PrusaSlicer) → G-code → print.
  • Use it for enclosures, sensor mounts, robot chassis and gears.
TermMeaning
FilamentPLA (easy), ABS (strong, heat resistant), PETG (tough)
Nozzle / bedPLA about 200 °C nozzle, 60 °C bed
Layer heighte.g. 0.2 mm; smaller is finer but slower
Infill15 to 20% for normal parts
SupportsTemporary structures under overhangs
Quick viva questions
  • What does a slicer do?
  • PLA vs ABS: which is easier and why?
  • What are supports for?
10Project

The project combines sensors, display, Bluetooth/app, cloud and a printed body into one working solution.

Key points

  • Draw a block diagram and circuit diagram first; test each module alone, then combine.
  • Keep a log: components, pin table, commented code, photos.
  • Report: Aim, Components, Block diagram, Circuit, Code, Working, Output, Conclusion, Future scope.
IdeaMain components
Smart dustbinUltrasonic, servo, Arduino
Bluetooth carHC-05, L298N, 2 DC motors, app
Weather monitorDHT11, LCD, ESP32, ThingSpeak
Street lightLDR, relay, LED
Parking assistantUltrasonic, buzzer, LCD
Quick viva questions
  • Does every module work alone?
  • Is the wiring neat and labelled?
  • Can you explain every line of code?
11Seminar / Presentation

The last session is presenting your work. A clear story matters as much as the working model.

Key points

  • One idea per slide, large text, more diagrams than paragraphs.
  • Show a live demo, with a short video as backup.
  • Practise to fit 5 to 8 minutes and speak to the audience.
  • Expect: why this sensor? what problem does it solve? biggest difficulty?
Quick viva questions
  • Slides saved on pen drive and email?
  • Hardware, cables, power packed?
  • Who explains what?
